meaning: regoshi, as for this summer [you told us about], how was it? natsu: summer

kanji: でもね私たちにはお金が必要なんだ
hiragana: でも ね わたしたち に は おかね が ひつよう なんだ
romaji: demo ne watashitachi ni ha okane ga hitsuyou nanda
meaning: [I know it's not nice] but we need money! hitsuyou: necessary; needed; essential; indispensable This is another interesting example of different word types: In Japanese, it's a noun, while you would rather use a verb (need) in English.

kanji: その後どうなったかは誰も知らねえ
hiragana: そのご どう なった か は だれ も しらねえ
romaji: sonogo dou natta ka ha dare mo shiranee
meaning: [What] happened afterwards, noone knows. sonogo: after that; afterwards (sometimes also pronounced "sonoato").

kanji: もっと上手になりたい
hiragana: もっと じょうず に なりたい
meaning: [I] want to become better [at this]. jouzu: skillful; skilled; proficient; good (at)

kanji: でもやっぱり人の血は必要
hiragana: でも やっぱり ひと の ち は ひつよう
romaji: demo yappari hito no chi ha hitsuyou
meaning: But as expected, human blood is a requirement -> we need human blood [to complete this / to heal him...] yappari. as expected; sure enough; after all (is said and done); in the end

hiragana: ね かみ すこし きったら
meaning: How about cutting [your] hair a bit? Literally: what if you cut your hair a bit (due to conditional form "kittara"). kiru: to cut (paper, hair, vegetables), but also: to hang up the phone

kanji: もっとお金が必要になるよ
hiragana: もっと おかね が ひつよう に なる よ
romaji: motto okane ga hitsuyou ni naru yo
meaning: [We] will need more money [to finish this].

kanji: 二人はあのシガンシナ区の出身だよね
hiragana: ふたり は あの しがんしなく の しゅっしん だ よ ね
romaji: futari ha ano shiganshinaku no shusshin da yo ne
meaning: As for you two, [you are] from shinganshinaku, aren't you? shusshin: one's origin (e.g. city, country, parentage, school) Remark: I found names quite hard to understand...

hiragana: ここ の ふゆ は いい な
romaji: koko no fuyu ha ii na
meaning: The winter here is great, isn't it? fuyu: winter

hiragana: みず と お といれ は した よ
romaji: mizu to o toire ha shita yo
meaning: Water and the toilet are downstairs -> the girl is renting a room in an old house. She doesn't have water and a toilet on this floor. shita: below; down; under
source: Kikis delivery service (魔女の宅急便)

kanji: さっきから何を気にしてるんだよ
hiragana: さっき から なに を き に してる ん だ よ
romaji: sakki kara nani wo ki ni shiteru n da yo
meaning: What do you mind since recently? -> What is bothering you since a while ago? ki ni suru: to mind (negative nuance); to care about I found it hard to distinguish all these phrases with "ki".

hiragana: そのあと の じょうほう は なし
meaning: As for after that, there's no information -> They are talking about a mysterious girl, but only know about her up so some point in time. sonoato: after that; afterwards (sometimes also pronounced "sonogo").

kanji: 黒いニャンコってかわいいな
hiragana: くろい にゃんこ って かわいい な
meaning: As for black cats, [they] are cute. kuroi: black, dark nyanko: kitty-cat (children's language). This is an important word in this anime, more on this later ;)

kanji: 別にお金をかける必要はないの
hiragana: べつ に おかね を かける ひつよう は ない の
romaji: betsu ni okane wo kakeru hitsuyou ha nai no
meaning: There's no need to spend money. betsuni: (not) particularly; (not) especially; (not) specially okane wo kakeru: to spend money

kanji: いいえそれは違います｡
hiragana: いいえ それ は ちがいます ｡
meaning: No, as for that, [it's] wrong. iie: no -> make sure to read the article I linked as reference

hiragana: しゅっしん どこ です か
meaning: As for [your origin], where is it? -> Where are you from? shusshin: one's origin (e.g. city, country, parentage, school)
source: Terrace House- Boys & Girls in the City

hiragana: まど を あけた の は だれ だ ?
romaji: mado wo aketa no ha dare da ?
meaning: As for opened the window: Who is it? -> Who opened the window? mado: window

kanji: でもどうして人を傷つける必要があるんだろう
hiragana: でも どうして ひと を きずつける ひつよう が ある ん だろう
romaji: demo doushite hito wo kizutsukeru hitsuyou ga aru n darou
meaning: But why is it necessary to wound / injure people?

kanji: それでみんなで結婚おめでとうって言いましょう
hiragana: それで みんな で けっこん おめでとう って いいましょう
romaji: sorede minna de kekkon omedetou tte iimashou
meaning: And now, let's say congratulations to [your] wedding with everybody! kekkon: marriage (this ranks surprisingly high on my frequency lists) sorede: so; therefore; and; (and) then, well

kanji: タケシじゃあその下の写真は
hiragana: たけし じゃあ その した の しゃしん は
romaji: takeshi jaa sono shita no shashin ha
meaning: Ok, and what about the picture below [the one you just explained? They are looking at a larger gallery of pictures on the wall]. shita: below; down; under

kanji: 全然感じが違いますよ
hiragana: ぜんぜん かんじ が ちがいます よ
meaning: The feeling / impression [when drinking ordinary grape juice and freshly pressed juice] is completely different (they are really talking about juice here :D). kanji: feeling; sense; impression The word "kanji" is not only a Chinese character, but it also has this completely different meaning. I often found this quite hard to translate.

kanji: お前は兄弟と離れてはいかん
hiragana: おまえ は きょうだい と はなれて は いかん
romaji: omae ha kyoudai to hanarete ha ikan
meaning: As for you, [you] must not be separated from your siblings. kyoudai: sibling(s), also: brothers Reminder: "-te ha ikanai" means "must not"

kanji: 大丈夫大丈夫まだ黒くない
hiragana: だいじょうぶ だいじょうぶ まだ くろくない
meaning: It's ok, it's ok, it's not black yet (they're talking about a silver spear. When it turns dark, the speaker will die - for whatever reason). This sentence can also mean: It's not dark (outside) yet, i.e. the sun is still shining a bit. kuroi: black, dark

kanji: いいえ違うあなたは誰なの
hiragana: いいえ ちがう あなた は だれ な の
romaji: iie chigau anata ha dare na no
meaning: [You are Elizabeth...wait] no, wrong. Who are you? iie: no -> make sure to read the article I linked as reference

kanji: 窓から何かが入ってきて
hiragana: まど から なに か が はいって きて
romaji: mado kara nani ka ga haitte kite
meaning: Something entered through the window and... [took pikachu]. Note that the past tense in this example comes from the second part of the sentence, which is missing here. This sentence is linked to the second one using the -te form. mado: window Reminder: -te iku and -te kuru direct the preceding verb (hairu - to enter) into a direction. kuru means, that the entering happens towards the speaker into the room.

kanji: まさかこんなことになるなんて
hiragana: まさか こんな こと に なる なんて
romaji: masaka konna koto ni naru nante
meaning: By no means [I expected] something like this [to happen]... "masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

kanji: 私も結婚する前はそんなだったなあ
hiragana: わたし も けっこん する まえ は そんな だった なあ
romaji: watashi mo kekkon suru mae ha sonna datta naa
meaning: I also was like that before [I] got married. kekkon: marriage (this ranks surprisingly high on my frequency lists)

kanji: お前さあ学校でいっつも１人で本読んでるよな
hiragana: おまえ さあ がっこう で いっつも ひとり で ほん よんでる よ な
romaji: omae saa gakkou de ittsumo hitori de hon yonderu yo na
meaning: You, at school [you] always read books alone, don't you. hon: book "hon" also works with the store suffix we already had: honya - book store.

kanji: 越智黒崎家の兄弟ケンカならあっちでやれ
hiragana: おち くろさきか の きょうだい けんか なら あっち で やれ
romaji: ochi kurosakika no kyoudai kenka nara acchi de yare
meaning: kurosakika brothers, if [you want to] fight, then [go] over there [out of the room]. kyoudai: sibling(s), also: brothers

kanji: 茂田の右をよく見ておけ
hiragana: しげた の みぎ を よく みて おけ
romaji: shigeta no migi wo yoku mite oke
meaning: Keep your eyes on shigeta's right, or more literal: Watch shigeta's right well. migi: right

hiragana: ことば に き を つけろ
meaning: Watch your tone (lit: pay attention to your words). kotoba: word, phrase; but also: language / way of speaking
source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

kanji: いつまでも子供のままと思わないでください
hiragana: いつ まで も こども の まま と おもわないで ください
romaji: itsu made mo kodomo no mama to omowanaide kudasai
meaning: Please don't think of me as a kid forever. kodomo: child, kid itsu made mo: forever, this is often taught as one word or phrase (itsumademo). Literally, it means something like "until even when". Reminder 1: "to omou" is used to "quote" and talk about the previous phrase in the sense: to think. It's related to "to iu". Reminder 2: mama is a noun and refers to a state. xxx no mama usually translates to "as xxx".
source: Daily Lives of High School Boys (Eng + Jp)

kanji: 俺がギター始めた時何やってたか覚えてる
hiragana: おれ が ぎたー はじめた とき なに やってた か おぼえてる
romaji: ore ga gita- hajimeta toki nani yatteta ka oboeteru
meaning: At the time when I started [to play] the guitar, [do you] remember what [I] did [physical action]? -> e.g. what he did to improve, playing an instrument is hard, after all. hajimeru: to start; to begin; to commence

kanji: それ返すためにわざわざ来たの
hiragana: それ かえす ために わざわざ きた の
romaji: sore kaesu tameni wazawaza kita no
meaning: [You] explicitly came here for returning that? tame ni: for; for the sake of; in order to In some resources, this is often covered as topic of its own, but not found in Tae Kim's guide. Probably, because it is just the common use case of "ni" as Tae Kim explained it: ni marks the preceding word as target of a verb or clause. In this case, the preceding word is "tame - sake, purpose".

kanji: 夏になると町は怖いほど静かになる
hiragana: なつ に なる と まち は こわい ほど しずか に なる
romaji: natsu ni naru to machi ha kowai hodo shizuka ni naru
meaning: When [it] becomes summer, the city becomes quiet to a scary degree. natsu: summer

kanji: お父さんお料理上手だからおいしいですよ
hiragana: おとうさん お りょうり じょうず だ から おいしい です よ
romaji: otousan o ryouri jouzu da kara oishii desu yo
meaning: [Your] father is good at food (=at cooking) so [eating at your place will be] tasty. jouzu: skillful; skilled; proficient; good (at)

kanji: 泳ぐこと嫌いになってしまいましたか
hiragana: およぐ こと きらい に なって しまいました か
romaji: oyogu koto kirai ni natte shimaimashita ka
meaning: [After this incident] did swimming thing become disliked? -> Do you hate swimming now? kirai: disliked; hated; disagreeable Reminder: -te shimau describes unintended actions, often with bad outcome.

kanji: んまさか自分で切るの
hiragana: ん まさか じぶん で きる の
romaji: n masaka jibun de kiru no
meaning: Huh? No way, you cut [your hair] yourself?! kiru: to cut (paper, hair, vegetables), but also (like in this example): to hang up the phone

kanji: 寒さに強いと冬でも風邪をひかない
hiragana: さむさ に つよい と ふゆ で も かぜ を ひかない
romaji: samusa ni tsuyoi to fuyu de mo kaze wo hikanai
meaning: If [you] are strong against coldness, [you will] not catch a cold even though [it is] winter. fuyu: winter kaze wo hiku: to catch a cold

kanji: これじゃ走るのは無理だな
hiragana: これ じゃ はしる の は むり だ な
romaji: kore ja hashiru no ha muri da na
meaning: As for running, [this is] impossible [now, looks like the girl is injured] hashiru: to run

kanji: じゃあその後はどうするんだ
hiragana: じゃあ そのあと は どう する ん だ
romaji: jaa sonoato ha dou suru n da
meaning: As for afterwards, what [will] you do? -> well, and what will you do afterwards? sonoato: after that; afterwards

kanji: 二人はどこの出身なの
hiragana: ふたり は どこ の しゅっしん な の
romaji: futari ha doko no shusshin na no
meaning: As for you two, where are you from? shusshin: one's origin (e.g. city, country, parentage, school)

kanji: 食うためじゃなく殺すために殺したんだよ
hiragana: くう ため じゃなく ころす ために ころした ん だ よ
romaji: kuu tame janaku korosu tameni koroshita n da yo
meaning: Not [for] eat purpose [I killed], for kill purpose [I] killed. tame ni: for; for the sake of; in order to In some resources, this is often covered as topic of its own, but not found in Tae Kim's guide. Probably, because it is just the common use case of "ni" as Tae Kim explained it: ni marks the preceding word as target of a verb or clause. In this case, the preceding word is "tame - sake, purpose".

hiragana: ぼく も うたう の は すき だ
romaji: boku mo utau no ha suki da
meaning: I also like to sing. utau: to sing

kanji: そんなことを言う人大嫌いです
hiragana: そんな こと を いう ひと だいきらい です
romaji: sonna koto wo iu hito daikirai desu
meaning: [I] hate saying-such-thing people -> I hate people who say such things. daikirai: strong dislike, hating

kanji: じゃ下の名前教えてください
hiragana: じゃ した の なまえ おしえて ください
romaji: ja shita no namae oshiete kudasai
meaning: Please tell me [your] given name. Remark: In Japanese, you usually address people with their last name. When writing down names, the last name is written first. Moreover, Japanese is traditionally written from top to bottom, so the given name is below the last name. That's why given name literally is "bottom name" in Japanese, have a look at the reference. shita: below; down; under

kanji: なんで一人で掃除してるんだ俺
hiragana: なんで ひとり で そうじ してる ん だ おれ
romaji: nande hitori de souji shiteru n da ore
meaning: Why am I cleaning up alone? -> This guy loves to clean and to do housework. However, he's currently on vacation in Okinawa with some friends who went to the beach without him. souji: cleaning; sweeping; dusting; scrubbing

kanji: さっきお兄さんを呼んでくるって言って走ってたんだ
hiragana: さっき おにいさん を よんで くる って いって はしってた ん だ
romaji: sakki oniisan wo yonde kuru tte itte hashitteta n da
meaning: A while ago [she] said: [I go and call my brother] and went off. hashiru: to run Difficult sentence, hints: tte itte is "to iu" in it's -te form. "xxx to iu" means "to say xxx". The -te form then links it to the next part of the sentence (hashitteta), which is from hashitte ita.

hiragana: まど から はなれてて
meaning: Stay away from the window...! mado: window hanareru: to be separated, to go away hanaretete: colloquial shortening of hanarete ite, ite being the -te form of "iru". So we have an enduring state here, hence the "stay away" in the translation.

hiragana: たとえば
meaning: tatoeba: for example

kanji: この傘よかったらあんた使ってよ
hiragana: この かさ よかったら あんた つかって よ
romaji: kono kasa yokattara anta tsukatte yo
meaning: This umbrella, if [you] like, you can use it. tsukau: to use (a tool, method, etc.); to make use of; to put to use

kanji: お母さんお父さんと結婚できて幸せだったから
hiragana: おかあさん おとうさん と けっこん できて しあわせ だった から
romaji: okaasan otousan to kekkon dekite shiawase datta kara
meaning: As for mom, [she] was happy because she could marry dad. kekkon: marriage (this ranks surprisingly high on my frequency lists) Reminder: The -te form can be used to express a reason, have a look at the reference.

kanji: 世界に２人しかいない感じしない
hiragana: せかい に ふたり しか いない かんじ しない
romaji: sekai ni futari shika inai kanji shinai
meaning: Doesn't [this] feel like there are only two people / the two of us in the world? (They are sitting together in an empty classroom). kanji: feeling; sense; impression The word "kanji" is not only a Chinese character, but it also has this completely different meaning. I often found this quite hard to translate.

kanji: もう少し大きい声で歌いなさい
hiragana: もうすこし おおきい こえ で うたい なさい
romaji: mousukoshi ookii koe de utai nasai
meaning: Sing with a slightly louder / larger voice. utau: to sing Reminder: verb stem + nasai = firm, but polite order

hiragana: まさか
meaning: No way! By no means [can this be true]! "masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

kanji: うんトイレ掃除とか上手だよな
hiragana: うん といれ そうじ とか じょうず だ よ な
romaji: un toire souji toka jouzu da yo na
meaning: [And you, ramuchi, you are] good at cleaning toilets, right? -> the guy is trying to compliment one of the girls. Probably not the right words :D souji: cleaning; sweeping; dusting; scrubbing
source: Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (Eng + Jp)

kanji: まさか本当に食べてないのか
hiragana: まさか ほんとうに たべてない の か
meaning: No way, [you are] really not eating [this delicious food]? "masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not)

kanji: そんなふうに考えてはいけないと思っていた
hiragana: そんな ふう に かんがえて は いけない と おもって いた
romaji: sonna fuu ni kangaete ha ikenai to omotte ita
meaning: [I] thought [you] must not think that way fuu: method; manner; way; style

hiragana: つかって くれ おれ の からだ を
romaji: tsukatte kure ore no karada wo
meaning: Do [me] the favor of using [it], my body [I mean]. tsukau: to use (a tool, method, etc.); to make use of; to put to use

kanji: 殺す前にぜひ聞きたいことがある
hiragana: ころす まえ に ぜひ ききたい こと が ある
romaji: korosu mae ni zehi kikitai koto ga aru
meaning: Before [I] kill [you], [I] by all means want to know thing is there -> there's something I want to know by all means, before I kill you. zehi: by all means; certainly; definitely
source: Legend of the Galactic Heroes (JP Eng) (Media Added)

kanji: はいみんな登録してくれてありがとう
hiragana: はい みんな とうろく して くれて ありがとう
romaji: hai minna touroku shite kurete arigatou
meaning: Ok, thanks everyone for giving me the favor of subscribing! touroku: registration, subscription; this is a word you'll often hear in youtube videos ;)

kanji: 話は以上だ聞いてくれてありがとう
hiragana: はなし は いじょう だ きいて くれて ありがとう
romaji: hanashi ha ijou da kiite kurete arigatou
meaning: As for conversation, that's all. Thank you for giving me the favor of listening. ijou: that's all; that is the end; the end Again a word I often found hard to translate, probably because a different meaning of "ijou" is "beyond, more than", see one of the next cards.

kanji: いつもこんな感じなの
hiragana: いつも こんな かんじ な の
meaning: Does [it] always feel like this? lit: Is [it] always this feeling? kanji: feeling; sense; impression The word "kanji" is not only a Chinese character, but it also has this completely different meaning. I often found this quite hard to translate.

kanji: 俺に言えることは以上だ
hiragana: おれ に いえる こと は いじょう だ
romaji: ore ni ieru koto ha ijou da
meaning: As for what-I-can-say thing, that's all -> This is all I can say. ijou: that's all; that is the end; the end Again a word I often found hard to translate, probably because a different meaning of "ijou" is "beyond, more than", see one of the next cards.

kanji: 待ってまさか本当に言いたいことがあるのか
hiragana: まって まさか ほんとうに いいたい こと が ある の か
romaji: matte masaka hontouni iitai koto ga aru no ka
meaning: Wait, you gotta be kidding, is there really something [you] want to say? "masaka" is not always easy to translate directly. It is very common though and usually means, that something is unbelievable and not likely to be true. The official dictionary definition is: by no means; never!; well, I never!; you don't say!; certainly (not) Reminder: iu (to say) -> iitai (want to say)

kanji: ありがとう今日聞きたかったことは以上です
hiragana: ありがとう きょう ききたかった こと は いじょう です
romaji: arigatou kyou kikitakatta koto ha ijou desu
meaning: Thank you. As for [what I] wanted to ask today thing, that's all -> this is all I wanted to ask you today. Note that "koto" can in many cases not be translated to English directly, but you'll get used to this over time, trust me ;). ijou: that's all; that is the end; the end Again a word I often found hard to translate, probably because a different meaning of "ijou" is "beyond, more than", see one of the next cards. Reminder: kiku -> kikitai -> kikitakatta (wanted to ask)

kanji: ちょっとそういう言い方は良くないよ
hiragana: ちょっと そういう いいかた は よくない よ
romaji: chotto souiu iikata ha yokunai yo
meaning: Come on, that way-of-saying is not good -> don't put it that way. souiu: such; like that; that sort of​ (refers to something close to the listener, just as for sore / kore)

kanji: だからってこんなふうに勝っても全然うれしくないよ
hiragana: だ から って こんな ふう に かって も ぜんぜん うれしくない よ
romaji: da kara tte konna fuu ni katte mo zenzen ureshikunai yo
meaning: ...but even if [I] win this way, it's totally not joyful/delightful -> I don't want to win like this [the speaker is about to win a fight, because the opponent gave up]. fuu: method; manner; way; style The pattern -te mo can be used to express: even if / regardless / no matter what.

kanji: これ以上なにをする気だ
hiragana: これ いじょう なに を する き だ
romaji: kore ijou nani wo suru ki da
meaning: Beyond this, what-do intention is it? This sort of means: What else do you intend to do beyond this? Do you want to cause even more trouble? ijou: beyond, more than ki: motivation, intention I'd say the major meaning of "ki" is "spirit; mind; heart​". What I found very interesting is that all other meanings such as "motivation, intention" can somehow be mapped to "spirit, mind".

kanji: 読めない漢字があったら教えてやるぞん
hiragana: よめない かんじ が あったら おしえて やる ぞん
romaji: yomenai kanji ga attara oshiete yaru zon
meaning: If there's a cannot-read kanji, [I] teach [you]. kanji: Chinese character, which makes reading Japanese a nightmare (or fun, choose your favorite :D) Note the -te yaru construction. Here, we do not have a physical action. Instead, this is used to express the listener's lower status. A more friendly way to express this would be to use -te ageru.

kanji: それを言うために待っていた
hiragana: それ を いう ために まって いた
romaji: sore wo iu tameni matte ita
meaning: [I] have been waiting for the purpose of telling [you] that. tame ni: for; for the sake of; in order to Here, tame is described by a clause (sore-wo-iu).
source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

kanji: こういうのは時間がかかる
hiragana: こういう の は じかん が かかる
romaji: kouiu no ha jikan ga kakaru
meaning: [Things] like this take time. kouiu: such; this sort of; like this (refers to something close to the speaker, just as for sore / kore)

kanji: 自分のことも嫌いにならないで
hiragana: じぶん の こと も きらい に ならない で
romaji: jibun no koto mo kirai ni naranai de
meaning: Don't start to hate yourself... kirai: disliked; hated; disagreeable Remark: "mo" is used for emphasis here, which is a frequent use case. Have a look at the references.

kanji: もっと走らせるべきだったか
hiragana: もっと はしらせる べき だった か
meaning: Should [I] have made them running more? -> Looks like the guy is a trainer, this anime is about running. hashiru: to run Reminder 1: hashiraseru is causative: to make or to let someone do something - running in this case. Reminder 2: beki is used to express "should"

kanji: 結局お前はそういう奴なんだ
hiragana: けっきょく おまえ は そういう やつ なんだ
romaji: kekkyoku omae ha souiu yatsu nanda
meaning: So in the end, you are that sort of person -> looks like the speaker just realized the true nature of the listener. souiu: such; like that; that sort of​ (refers to something close to the listener, just as for sore / kore)

kanji: 大丈夫お腹お腹痛いの
hiragana: だいじょうぶ おなか おなか いたい の
meaning: [Are you] Ok? Stomach? Does [your] stomach hurt? onaka: stomach, belly

kanji: ダメだダメだこれ以上考えるな
hiragana: だめ だ だめ だ これ いじょう かんがえる な
romaji: dame da dame da kore ijou kangaeru na
meaning: It's bad, it's bad, do not think about [it] beyond this point [i.e. do not think any further].

kanji: しまった俺のノドがあがああ
hiragana: しまった おれ の のど が あ が ああ
romaji: shimatta ore no nodo ga a ga aa
meaning: Damn it, my throat, grwafawr -> Sounds like the poor guy gets choked by something... nodo: throat
source: JoJos Bizarre Adventure 黄金の風 (26-39)

hiragana: どうしたん だ それ は
meaning: What happened? As for that [you in this small jar, I mean] doushitan: what happened? What's the matter? This actually is: dou shita no with the last "no" just as "n". Literally, it means: what/how was [it] (from dou shita), the additional "no" is the explanatory one, which in a question means that an explanation is desired. Caution, this is rather informal.

hiragana: いっしゅうかん くらい まえ か な
meaning: [It was] about one week ago, wasn't it? kurai: approximately, about, around (sometimes also spelled "gurai", used to make expressions or numbers more vague) isshuukan: one week Just learn isshuukan as "one week" for now. This is actually build from: ichi - one shuu - week kan - period of time I found counting boring and a nighmare for several reasons, every 5 year old Japanese kid can probably do it better than me. This will be put into a separate deck.
source: からかい上手の高木さん

kanji: どうして英語で歌ってくれないんですか
hiragana: どうして えいご で うたって くれない ん です か
romaji: doushite eigo de utatte kurenai n desu ka
meaning: Why don't [you] sing in English [for me]? utau: to sing

kanji: 試合が終わったなんてまだ信じられないや
hiragana: しあい が おわった なんて まだ しんじられない や
romaji: shiai ga owatta nante mada shinjirarenai ya
meaning: That the match is over, [I] still can't believe (maybe it was a fight against a very tough opponent) shiai: match, game. Sometimes also: fight

kanji: こういう顔のいい男だ
hiragana: こういう かお の いい おとこ だ
romaji: kouiu kao no ii otoko da
meaning: [The guy I am referring to] is a nice man with a face like this [look at the picture the speaker has drawn: Very accurate :D] kouiu: such; this sort of; like this (refers to something close to the speaker, just as for sore / kore)

kanji: 大掃除がそんなに楽しいのかよ
hiragana: おおそうじ が そんなに たのしい の か よ
romaji: oosouji ga sonnani tanoshii no ka yo
meaning: Is new year's cleaning really that fun?! souji: cleaning; sweeping; dusting; scrubbing oosouji: major cleanup, spring cleanup (new year's cleaning often done in Japanese households in late December)

hiragana: くすり あけて あげよう か
meaning: Shall [I] give [you] the favor of opening the medicine? The guy on the bed maybe does not have enough strength to open it himself. kusuri: medicine
source: The World God Only Knows S3 (jp eng)

kanji: 明日も同じ時間に勉強よ
hiragana: あした も おなじ じかん に べんきょう よ
romaji: ashita mo onaji jikan ni benkyou yo
meaning: Tomorrow too [we] study at the same time.

kanji: お腹いっぱいになったからちょっと休憩
hiragana: おなか いっぱい に なった から ちょっと きゅうけい
romaji: onaka ippai ni natta kara chotto kyuukei
meaning: Because [I] became so full, [I will] take a break. onaka: stomach, belly onaka ippai: colloquial way to say you're full, also: that you had enough.

kanji: ただいまお母さんお茶喉からから
hiragana: ただいま おかあさん おちゃ のど から から
romaji: tadaima okaasan ocha nodo kara kara
meaning: [I] am home! Mom! Tea! [My] throat is bone dry nodo: throat karakara: parched, bone dry. This is a nice example for onomatopoeia (words that mimic something): karakara sounds a bit like choking or a dry throat, doesn't it?

hiragana: じゃあ じこしょうかい して
meaning: Introduce yourself jikoshoukai: self-introduction. It's jiko + shoukai. We already had it in several videos, here's finally a flashcard as reminder ;).

kanji: 今私信じられないくらいに幸せです
hiragana: いま わたし しんじられない くらい に しあわせ です
romaji: ima watashi shinjirarenai kurai ni shiawase desu
meaning: Now [I am] happy to the can't believe-extend kurai: approximately, about, around (sometimes also spelled "gurai", used to make expressions or numbers more vague) kurai: to (about) the extend that...

hiragana: ことし は きびしそう だ よ
meaning: Looks like winning will be hard this year. kotoshi: this year, current year kibishii: severe; strict; rigid; unsparing; relentless Reminder: -sou: appearing that; seeming that; looking like; having the appearance This is just another example for expressing similarity/appearance/hearsay. Don't worry about the difference to the others for now, just translate it like the others.
source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

kanji: これ以上戦うのは無理だ
hiragana: これ いじょう たたかう の は むり だ
romaji: kore ijou tatakau no ha muri da
meaning: Fighting beyond this is impossible.

kanji: 私あの試合テレビで見てました
hiragana: わたし あの しあい てれび で みてました
romaji: watashi ano shiai terebi de mitemashita
meaning: I saw that [special] match on TV shiai: match, game. Sometimes also: fight

kanji: どうしたのそんな暗い顔して
hiragana: どう した の そんな くらい かお して
romaji: dou shita no sonna kurai kao shite
meaning: What's wrong? Making such a dark face? doushitano / dou shita no: what's the matter?; what's wrong? kurai: dark, gloomy (don't mix them up...) I already mentioned it on a different card: Japanese has many homophones (words with same pronunciation, but different meaning). They are usually written with different kanji - one of the strengths of the writing system. Since there are no kanji popping up during a conversation however, this will not help your listening comprehension much.
source: Terrace House- Boys & Girls in the City

kanji: これからは毎年やろうね
hiragana: これから は まいとし やろう ね
meaning: From now on, let's do this [physical action] every year. maitoshi: every year

kanji: 俺は薬を飲むのを止めた
hiragana: おれ は くすり を のむ の を やめた
romaji: ore ha kusuri wo nomu no wo yameta
meaning: As for me, [I] stopped drinking the medicine kusuri: medicine

kanji: 私が代わりに行ってきてやる
hiragana: わたし が かわり に いって きて やる
romaji: watashi ga kawari ni itte kite yaru
meaning: I give you (lower rank) the favor of going instead. kawari: substitute; replacement; substituting; replacing kawari ni: instead of, as substitute for Reminder: -te yaru has the meaning of -te ageru (doing something for someone directed away from the speaker), but is used for something of lower rank, e.g. when feeding your dog. When used among people, it's rather unfriendly. Here, the cat is speaking. The cat actually thinks of itself as noble being and thus adresses the protagonist as inferior.

kanji: 結構お姉さんっぽいですよ
hiragana: けっこう おねえさん っぽい です よ
meaning: [This is] pretty older sister-ish (someone wants to act like a larger sister here). kekkou: quite, reasonably, fairly, pretty ppoi: -ish, (slang)

kanji: 早く帰らないと雨降ってくるわよ
hiragana: はやく かえらない と あめ ふって くる わ よ
romaji: hayaku kaeranai to ame futte kuru wa yo
meaning: [You] must come home fast, rain will come falling (less literal: it will rain) furu: to fall (rain, snow, NOT falling of a person, this is ochiru)

hiragana: きょう は それ で けっこう
meaning: As for today, this is well enough (lit: [we are] well enough with this -> we don't need to do more today). kekkou: well enough, ok, tolerable (one of these words with different meanings, I somehow found it hard to learn)

kanji: 明るいときもあれば暗いときもある
hiragana: あかるい とき も あれば くらい とき も ある
romaji: akarui toki mo areba kurai toki mo aru
meaning: If there are bright times, there are also dark times. Just ignore the first "mo" here.

kanji: この雨は普通の雨じゃない
hiragana: この あめ は ふつう の あめ じゃない
romaji: kono ame ha futsuu no ame janai
meaning: As for this rain, [it] is no normal rain (maybe it is raining more than usual). futsuu: normal; ordinary; regular

kanji: もう一つもらっていいですか
hiragana: もうひとつ もらって いい です か
meaning: Can [I] get another one? mouhitotsu: another one

kanji: いつもあたしに力をくれた
hiragana: いつも あたし に ちから を くれた
romaji: itsumo atashi ni chikara wo kureta
meaning: [Thank you, you] always gave me power. atashi: girl / female version of "watashi"

kanji: 海なんて毎年来てんだから
hiragana: うみ なんて まいとし きてん だ から
romaji: umi nante maitoshi kiten da kara
meaning: [Don't worry, I can safely run around here] because [we] come to this ocean every year [the listener is worried that the speaker might hurt himself running around on the beach]. maitoshi: every year

kanji: 予定より早く着いちゃったからな
hiragana: よてい より はやく ついちゃった から な
romaji: yotei yori hayaku tsuichatta kara na
meaning: We arrived earlier here than planned. yotei: plans; arrangement; schedule

hiragana: だいじょうぶ きょう も やすむ
meaning: [Are you] OK? [You] also take a rest today? yasumu: to take a rest, to take a day off, to be absent

kanji: どうしてそういうことするの
hiragana: どうして そういう こと する の
meaning: Why are you doing that?! souiu: such; like that; that sort of​ (refers to something close to the listener, just as for sore / kore)

kanji: あれは普通の女の子じゃないけど
hiragana: あれ は ふつう の おんなのこ じゃない けど
romaji: are ha futsuu no onnanoko janai kedo
meaning: As for that [over there, it is] not a normal girl.

kanji: 雨が降ってる時に傘を忘れるバカがどこにいるの
hiragana: あめ が ふってる ときに かさ を わすれる ばか が どこ に いる の
romaji: ame ga futteru tokini kasa wo wasureru baka ga doko ni iru no
meaning: Where [in the world] is an idiot, who forgets an umbrella at the time it is raining -> what the speaker wants to express: there's noone in the world who forgets an umbrella when it rains furu: to fall (rain, snow, NOT falling of a person, this is ochiru)

hiragana: め さめた か
meaning: Are [you] awake? Literally: did your eyes wake up? sameru: to wake, to wake up me ga sameru: to wake up (sameru is often used like this, i.e. together with me - eyes)

kanji: 私ね見えてることもう１つあるよ
hiragana: わたし ね みえてる こと もうひとつ ある よ
romaji: watashi ne mieteru koto mouhitotsu aru yo
meaning: There's one other thing I can see (one other thing in the personality of the listener, that's what they are currently talking about). mouhitotsu: another one

kanji: いつ目覚めるのか目覚めたとき俺はどうすればいいのか
hiragana: いつ めざめる の か めざめた とき おれ は どう すれば いい の か
romaji: itsu mezameru no ka mezameta toki ore ha dou sureba ii no ka
meaning: When [do you] wake up? At wakeup time as for me, what shoud [I] do -> what should I do when you wake up? mezameru: to wake up (I'm not a linguist, but I'd say this is a standalone word resulting from me ga sameru without the "ga").

kanji: でもいくらぐらいかかるのかな
hiragana: でも いくら ぐらい かかる の か な
romaji: demo ikura gurai kakaru no ka na
meaning: But [I wonder] how much [it] costs. "kurai" is sometimes spelled "gurai"

kanji: でもこういう仕事も勉強になるよ
hiragana: でも こういう しごと も べんきょう に なる よ
romaji: demo kouiu shigoto mo benkyou ni naru yo
meaning: But a job like this even will become study / experience [for you] -> you will learn a lot from this job. kouiu: such; this sort of; like this (refers to something close to the speaker, just as for sore / kore)

kanji: この世界だと髪洗うのも大変だし
hiragana: この せかい だ と かみ あらう の も たいへん だ し
romaji: kono sekai da to kami arau no mo taihen da shi
meaning: If it is this world (i.e. if we're in this world), even washing my hair is difficult. -> This is from Dr. Stone, where civilization was turned to stone somehow. Maybe they're lacking water... arau: to wash If "da to" confuses you: it's really just da + to, meaning "if it is x, then y"

kanji: 羽川さん今日は学校を休みなさい私も休むから
hiragana: はねがわ さんきょう は がっこう を やすみ なさい わたし も やすむ から
romaji: hanegawa sankyou ha gakkou wo yasumi nasai watashi mo yasumu kara
meaning: Hanegawa-san, take the day off from school, I also take a rest (ignore the trailing "kara" here). yasumu: to be absent; to take a day off, to rest

kanji: うん思ったより普通だね
hiragana: うん おもった より ふつう だ ね
romaji: un omotta yori futsuu da ne
meaning: Yes, [it is really not a special item. It is] more normal than [I] thought.

kanji: そしてまた俺は夢から覚める
hiragana: そして また おれ は ゆめ から さめる
romaji: soshite mata ore ha yume kara sameru
meaning: And then, I wake up from [this] dream -> The speaker seems to dream this dream often and always wakes up when something happens. sameru: to wake, to wake up

kanji: 駅まで一緒に歩いただけですう
hiragana: えき まで いっしょ に あるいた だけ ですう
romaji: eki made issho ni aruita dake desuu
meaning: [We] just walked to the station together! eki: train station

kanji: ちょっと喉が痛いだけだから
hiragana: ちょっと のど が いたい だけ だ から
romaji: chotto nodo ga itai dake da kara
meaning: [It's nothing, don't worry] because it's just my throat that hurts a bit. nodo: throat

kanji: すごい楽しかったよ普通に
hiragana: すごい たのしかった よ ふつう に
meaning: [I don't know why I am bored. Going to the cinema used to be] very enjoyable. Normally [I mean]. futsuu ni: normally
source: Terrace House-Boys x Girls Next Door

kanji: 小林体洗うのはその体の方がやりやすいんじゃないの
hiragana: こばやし からだ あらう の は その からだ の ほう が やり やすい ん じゃない の
romaji: kobayashi karada arau no ha sono karada no hou ga yari yasui n janai no
meaning: As for washing [your] body: Isn't that [other] body easier? -> The listener can change her body shape and the speaker wonders, if washing her body in a given shape is easier. arau: to wash

kanji: 見えなくても感じられる
hiragana: みえなくて も かんじられる
meaning: Even if [you] do not see [him, you] can feel [his presence]. The pattern -te mo can be used to express: even if / regardless / no matter what.

kanji: 早く家の中に入りなさい
hiragana: はやく いえ の なか に はいり なさい
romaji: hayaku ie no naka ni hairi nasai
meaning: Quickly get inside the house naka: inside; interior; among; within

hiragana: くすり ぜんぶ のんだ の か
meaning: Did [you] drink ALL of the medicine?! Note the small break behind "zenbu", which illustrates the use: xxx-zenbu means all of xxx. kusuri: medicine

kanji: 君が逃げても死にます
hiragana: きみ が にげて も しにます
meaning: Even if you escape, [you will] die.
source: 今からあなたを脅迫します

kanji: コンビニでバイトしてた駅前の
hiragana: こんびに で ばいと してた えきまえ の
romaji: konbini de baito shiteta ekimae no
meaning: [He] worked part time at the convenience store. The one in front of the train station. eki: train station

hiragana: そして ことし とき は きた
meaning: ...and this year, the time [for this] has come. kotoshi: this year, current year

kanji: 私が女にモテるのは何でだと思う
hiragana: わたし が おんな に もてる の は なんで だ と おもう
romaji: watashi ga onna ni moteru no ha nande da to omou
meaning: Why do [you] think I am so popular among girls? moteru: to be popular (esp. with the opposite sex); to be well liked

kanji: 今までこんな夢をあまり見たことがなかった
hiragana: いま まで こんな ゆめ を あまり みた こと が なかった
romaji: ima made konna yume wo amari mita koto ga nakatta
meaning: Until now, [I] didn't see such a dream very often -> I didn't dream a dream like this very often until now. amari: (not) very; (not) much; sometimes, also "anmari", which is more colloquial, see ref.

kanji: 今年は映画を作るみたいなんだけど
hiragana: ことし は えいが を つくる みたい なんだ けど
romaji: kotoshi ha eiga wo tsukuru mitai nanda kedo
meaning: This year, it seems like [they] are making a movie [at the school's culture festival]. A culture festival is an event held by many schools, where students show some kind of artistic achievement. This is also topic of various animes. kotoshi: this year, current year

kanji: なるほどよく見れば男だ
hiragana: なるほど よく みれば おとこ だ
meaning: [Now I] get it. If [I] look closely, [you are] a guy. The guy in this scene often is mistaken for his grandma for various reasons. The conversation continues on the next card...

kanji: 目を閉じるとまだ夢の中にいるみたい
hiragana: め を とじる と まだ ゆめ の なか に いる みたい
romaji: me wo tojiru to mada yume no naka ni iru mitai
meaning: When [I] close [my] eyes, it seems like [I] am still inside this dream. naka: inside; interior; among; within

kanji: よく見なくても男だよ
hiragana: よく みなくて も おとこ だ よ
romaji: yoku minakute mo otoko da yo
meaning: Even if [you] do not look closely, [I] am a guy! Just before, the cat said to the guy: [Now I] get it. If [I] look closely, [you are] a guy. The pattern -te mo can be used to express: even if / regardless / no matter what.

kanji: 相変わらずすごい人気ね
hiragana: あいかわらず すごい にんき ね
meaning: [He is] popular as ever, isn't [he]? ninki: popularity; public favor

kanji: ありがとうそれ食べ終わったら帰ってね
hiragana: ありがとう それ たべ おわったら かえって ね
romaji: arigatou sore tabe owattara kaette ne
meaning: When [you] finished eathing this, go home. Every once in a while you might encounter verbs that are not chained together using the -te form, but the verb stem (tabe in this case) followed by another verb. Just have a look at wasabi jpn's explanation.

kanji: 食べ終わったら電車で帰ろうね
hiragana: たべ おわったら でんしゃ で かえろう ね
romaji: tabe owattara densha de kaerou ne
meaning: When [you] finished eathing this, let's go home by train. Every once in a while you might encounter verbs that are not chained together using the -te form, but the verb stem (tabe) followed by another verb. I could not find any official rules here, only a question on Japanese stack exchange, but I think the answer does not apply here. Just accept it for now, the examples are rather rare. I still wanted to add this for the sake of completeness.

kanji: 僕にできることがあまり分からないけど
hiragana: ぼく に できる こと が あまり わからない けど
romaji: boku ni dekiru koto ga amari wakaranai kedo
meaning: [I'd love to do something about it] but as for things that can be done by me, [I] don't understand much [about them] -> I don't know what I can do. amari: (not) very; (not) much

hiragana: わたし も そと で あそびたい
meaning: I also want to play outside. soto: outside, exterior

kanji: 長い時間一緒に過ごしてきたよな
hiragana: ながい じかん いっしょ に すごして きた よ な
romaji: nagai jikan issho ni sugoshite kita yo na
meaning: It came [that we] spent a long time together... sugosu: to pass (time); to spend

kanji: 今あなたと話すか話さないか決めた
hiragana: いま あなた と はなす か はなさない か きめた
romaji: ima anata to hanasu ka hanasanai ka kimeta
meaning: [He] just decided if [he] either talks or not talks to you. Or less literally: He just decided if he talks to you or not. x ka y ka: Either x or y. Especially if y is the negation of x as in this example, this can also be translated to "whether or not".

kanji: じゃあ興味あるかないかまだ分かんない感じ
hiragana: じゃあ きょうみ ある か ない か まだ わかんない かんじ
romaji: jaa kyoumi aru ka nai ka mada wakannai kanji
meaning: Well, it feels like [he] still doesn't know if [he] has interest [in it] or not. x ka y ka: Either x or y. Especially if y is the negation of x as in this example, this can also be translated to "whether or not".

kanji: いいか生きるか死ぬかの勝負と思え
hiragana: いい か いきる か しぬ か の しょうぶ と おもえ
romaji: ii ka ikiru ka shinu ka no shoubu to omoe
meaning: DID YOU GET THIS?! THINK [about it] AS MATCH/CONTEST OF EITHER LIVING OR DYING! x ka y ka: Either x or y. Reminder: omoe is the (rather rude) command form of omou - to think. ikiru: to live, to exist

kanji: なんでみんなに告白するの
hiragana: なんで みんな に こくはく する の
romaji: nande minna ni kokuhaku suru no
meaning: Why do [you] confess [your] love to everyone? kokuhaku: professing one's feelings (to someone one wants to go out with); declaration of love This word is pretty frequent in anime, but not so common on the wikipedia frequency list i'm using ;).
source: The World God Only Knows S3 (jp eng)

kanji: おすごい軽くて人気のやつじゃん
hiragana: お すごい かるくて にんき の やつ じゃん
romaji: o sugoi karukute ninki no yatsu jan
meaning: [This firetable on the picture] is the thing that's so popular, because it is so light -> this anime is about camping, and on some campgrounds, people are not allowed to light a campfire directly on the ground. ninki: popularity; public favor

kanji: 小木曽と付き合うのか
hiragana: おぎそ と つきあう の か
meaning: [Do you] go out with ogiso? tsukiau: to keep company with; to go out with. This is often used in the context of dating, but is not restricted to this use case.

kanji: おいしいかどうか分からないけど
hiragana: おいしい か どう か わからない けど
romaji: oishii ka dou ka wakaranai kedo
meaning: [I know I should eat this] but [I] don't know whether or not [it] is tasty. xxx ka dou ka: whether or not something is xxx

kanji: やっぱり私たちも学校の外探しに行こうよ
hiragana: やっぱり わたしたち も がっこう の そと さがし に いこう よ
romaji: yappari watashitachi mo gakkou no soto sagashi ni ikou yo
meaning: I knew it! We should also go to search [for it] outside of the school. soto: outside, exterior
source: Sakurasou no Pet na Kanojo (jp eng)

kanji: 私も両親も同じ気持ちだった
hiragana: わたし も りょうしん も おなじ きもち だった
romaji: watashi mo ryoushin mo onaji kimochi datta
meaning: Both I and my parents had the same feeling. x mo y mo: Both x and y

kanji: この夏私と過ごしてどうだった
hiragana: この なつ わたし と すごして どう だった
romaji: kono natsu watashi to sugoshite dou datta
meaning: Spending this summer with me, how was it? sugosu: to pass (time); to spend
source: Ore no Imouto ga konna ni Kawaii Wake ga Nai_

kanji: 顔洗ったほうがいいですよ｡ はぁ
hiragana: かお あらった ほう が いい です よ ｡ はぁ
romaji: kao aratta hou ga ii desu yo ｡ haa
meaning: [You'd] better wash [your] face arau: to wash
source: Rascal Does Not Dream of a Dreaming Girl (Eng + Jp)

kanji: 覚えているかな俺に告白してくれたときのこと
hiragana: おぼえて いる か な おれ に こくはく して くれた とき の こと
romaji: oboete iru ka na ore ni kokuhaku shite kureta toki no koto
meaning: Are [you] remembering? The time when [you] gave me the favor of confessing [your] love... kokuhaku: professing one's feelings (to someone one wants to go out with); declaration of love

kanji: もういいお前も妹も殺してやる
hiragana: もう いい おまえ も いもうと も ころして やる
romaji: mou ii omae mo imouto mo koroshite yaru
meaning: That's enough, [I will] kill both you and your sister. x mo y mo: Both x and y Important: the "-te yaru" construction here does not mean "to do something for someone inferior", as we have learned in the section on giving and receiving. It has the second meaning of "(proactively) performing an action so as to prove one's ability to others." See discussion on Japanese stackexchange.

hiragana: くるま に き を つけて ね
romaji: kuruma ni ki wo tsukete ne
meaning: Pay attention to cars kuruma: car, vehicle

kanji: 見たことも聞いたこともない
hiragana: みた こと も きいた こと も ない
romaji: mita koto mo kiita koto mo nai
meaning: [I] have neither seen nor heard [about this]. x mo y mo: Neither x nor y (in a negative sentence)

kanji: 少し付き合ってくれないか
hiragana: すこし つきあって くれない か
meaning: Can [you] give [me] the favor of hanging out a bit? --> the speaker wants to talk to the protagonist of this anime, thus asks this question. tsukiau: to keep company with; to go out with. This is often used in the context of dating, but is not restricted to this use case.

kanji: 今日は私駅前で買い物して帰ります
hiragana: きょう は わたし えきまえ で かいもの して かえります
romaji: kyou ha watashi ekimae de kaimono shite kaerimasu
meaning: As for today, [I] go shopping in front of the train station. eki: train station

kanji: 怖いよ怖くてたまらないよ
hiragana: こわい よ こわくて たまらない よ
meaning: It's scary [in here]. It's scary and [I] can't stand it. tamaranai: unbearable, irresistible You can think of this word as "unbearable" in both a positive and negative sense: A scary situation is unbearable, but the lure of e.g. some delicious food might also be unbearable (we usually use something like irresistible in this case - see next card)

kanji: フッフフこれはたまらないな
hiragana: ふっふふ これ は たまらない な
meaning: [This food] is irresistible. This anime is about food and cooking, it's funny and weird btw. make sure to watch the first episode :D tamaranai: unbearable, irresistible You can think of this word as "unbearable" in both a positive and negative sense: A scary situation is unbearable, but the lure of e.g. some delicious food might also be unbearable.

kanji: そんなことをしたら刺すわよ
hiragana: そんな こと を したら さす わ よ
romaji: sonna koto wo shitara sasu wa yo
meaning: If [you] do that [running away leaving the speaker with his work behind] [I] will stab you. sasu: to stab, to sting

kanji: 俺が欲しいものは今も昔も変わらない
hiragana: おれ が ほしい もの は いま も むかし も かわらない
romaji: ore ga hoshii mono ha ima mo mukashi mo kawaranai
meaning: As for the thing I want: It changed neither now nor a long time ago (i.e. I still want the same). x mo y mo: Both x and y

kanji: ことみくんは私について何か言っていたかね
hiragana: ことみ くん は わたし に ついて なに か いって いた か ね
romaji: kotomi kun ha watashi ni tsuite nani ka itte ita ka ne
meaning: As for kotomi kun: Was [he] saying anything about me? xxx ni tsuite: about xxx, regarding xxx

hiragana: しんぱい する な すぐ ...
meaning: Don't worry... Reminder: The negative command form simply is verb + na, just as in this example. Try to keep this in mind for the next cards (negative command form).

kanji: その話どれくらい続くの
hiragana: その はなし どれ くらい つづく の
romaji: sono hanashi dore kurai tsudzuku no
meaning: As for that conversation, how long is it going to continue? tsudzuku: to continue; to last; to go on

kanji: 本当の問題は私の中にある
hiragana: ほんとう の もんだい は わたし の なか に ある
romaji: hontou no mondai ha watashi no naka ni aru
meaning: The real problem is inside me (probably something on her mind or her way of thinking) naka: inside; interior; among; within

kanji: うまるよーしお兄ちゃんいっぱい写真を撮ろう
hiragana: うまる よーし お にいちゃん いっぱい しゃしん を とろう
romaji: umaru yo-shi o niichan ippai shashin wo torou
meaning: Ok, big brother, let's take many pictures toru: to take (this is the most general of its 5000 meanings). shashin/video/podcast wo toru means to take/record a photo/video/podcast

kanji: もっとこの車のこと知りたいです
hiragana: もっと この くるま の こと しりたい です
romaji: motto kono kuruma no koto shiritai desu
meaning: [I] want to learn more about this car! kuruma: car, vehicle
source: The World God Only Knows S1 (jp eng)

hiragana: それ を わすれる な !
meaning: Don't forget this! Reminder: The negative command form simply is verb + na, just as in this example. Try to keep this in mind for the next cards (negative command form).

kanji: 料理を作ってくださるのは奥さんでしょ
hiragana: りょうり を つくって くださる の は おくさん でしょ
romaji: ryouri wo tsukutte kudasaru no ha okusan desho
meaning: As for giving [us] the favor of preparing food, it's your wife I guess? -> I guess your wife makes food for us? okusan: wife -te kudasaru has the same meaning as -te kureru, but is kind of one level more polite.
source: Legend of the Galactic Heroes (JP Eng) (Media Added)

kanji: 芽衣お弁当は２人で食べなさい
hiragana: めい おべんとう は ふたり で たべ なさい
romaji: mei obentou ha futari de tabe nasai
meaning: As for bento / (boxed) lunch, eat [it] together. Reminder: nasai: Use it together with the verb stem to issue a friendly yet firm command.

hiragana: で でも さしたら ち が
meaning: But if [I] stab it, blood... [will come out ->they are talking about killing a rabbit, but the speaker is afraid of blood] sasu: to stab, to sting
source: The Rising of the Shield Hero S1 [Eng Jp]

kanji: でもちょっとだけ食べなね
hiragana: でも ちょっと だけ たべ な ね
romaji: demo chotto dake tabe na ne
meaning: [You might not be hungry] but eat only a little bit. verb stem + na: colloquial abbreviation of "verb stem + nasai", i.e. tabe nasai in this case. This actually is a positive command, which confused me a lot - it is very similar to the negative command, after all. Here's the difference: negative command form: verb + na (e.g. taberu na)casual positive command: verb stem + na (e.g. tabe na, short for tabe nasai)

kanji: いつまでも続くとは思っていませんでしたしいつかは終わることですし
hiragana: いつ まで も つづく と は おもって いません でした し いつか は おわる こと です し
romaji: itsu made mo tsudzuku to ha omotte imasen deshita shi itsuka ha owaru koto desu shi
meaning: [I] didn't think that [it] lasts forever. [It] is a thing that ends someday... tsudzuku: to continue; to last; to go on

kanji: パンダくんほらもっと食べなよ
hiragana: ぱんだ くん ほら もっと たべ な よ
romaji: panda kun hora motto tabe na yo
meaning: Hey, come on, Panda, eat more! verb stem + na: colloquial abbreviation of "verb stem + nasai", i.e. tabe nasai in this case. This actually is a positive command, which confused me a lot - it is very similar to the negative command, after all. Here's the difference: negative command form: verb + na (e.g. taberu na)casual positive command: verb stem + na (e.g. tabe na, short for tabe nasai)

kanji: いつまでこの仕事を続けるつもりですか
hiragana: いつ まで この しごと を つづける つもり です か
romaji: itsu made kono shigoto wo tsudzukeru tsumori desu ka
meaning: Until when is [your] intention to continue this work? -> how long do you intend to continue this work? tsudsukeru: to continue Do you remember tsudzuku? It also means "to continue". The difference is: tsudzukeru is done by an active agent (e.g. a person), while tsudzuku happens passively. The first is called transitive, the second intransitive. Don't worry about the differences.

kanji: 上原携帯忘れたから取りに来たんだよ
hiragana: うえはら けいたい わすれた から とり に きたん だ よ
romaji: uehara keitai wasureta kara tori ni kitan da yo
meaning: Because [I] forgot [my] phone, [I] came to pick [it] up / take it with me toru: to take (this is the most general of its 5000 meanings). shashin/video/podcast wo toru means to take/record a photo/video/podcast

kanji: あっそうヴィルヘルムさんきれいな奥さんがいるって前に言ってたなと
hiragana: あっそう ゔぃるへるむ さん きれい な おくさん が いる って まえ に いってた な と
romaji: assou vyiruherumu san kirei na okusan ga iru tte mae ni itteta na to
meaning: Oh, right! Wilhelm san earlier said, he had a beautiful wife... okusan: wife
source: Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu (Eng + Jp)

kanji: もうあまり時間がありません
hiragana: もう あまり じかん が ありません
meaning: [I] don't have much time anymore. amari: (not) very; (not) much mou: already; (not) anymore (in a negative sentence)

kanji: 朝から晩までやってます
hiragana: あさ から ばん まで やってます
meaning: [I] do [this] from morning to evening [so I don't have time for club activities - the listener asked her to join a school club]. ban: evening

kanji: 今じゃ町は夜でも明るいしもう会うこともないかもな
hiragana: いま じゃ まち は よる でも あかるい し もう あう こと も ない かも な
romaji: ima ja machi ha yoru demo akarui shi mou au koto mo nai kamo na
meaning: These days, the city is bright even during night time (among other things), so we might not meet him (this anime is about supernatural beings, maybe there's one who only comes out when it is dark). yoru: evening; night

kanji: もし外で会ったらすぐ逃げること
hiragana: もし そと で あったら すぐ にげる こと
romaji: moshi soto de attara sugu nigeru koto
meaning: If [you] encounter [this animal] outside, run away. soto: outside, exterior
source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

kanji: おいしいですかよく食べるな｡
hiragana: おいしい です か よく たべる な ｡
romaji: oishii desu ka yoku taberu na ｡
meaning: Is it tasty? [You] eat well, don't you! ...and then there was of course the "taberu na" that is not a negative command (listen to the way this is pronounced). "na" is a sentence ending particle here, see ref below.

kanji: 親に迷惑をかけたくない
hiragana: おや に めいわく を かけたくない
meaning: [I] do not want to cause trouble for [my] parents. oya: parents; mother and father​

kanji: 今日の晩ご飯何がいいですか
hiragana: きょう の ばんごはん なに が いい です か
romaji: kyou no bangohan nani ga ii desu ka
meaning: As for today's dinner, what is good? -> what do you want to eat? bangohan: dinner

kanji: ほら口開けて見てください
hiragana: ほら くち あけて みて ください
meaning: Hey, try opening [your] mouth! kuchi: mouth, also: way of speaking
source: Ouran High School Host Club (jp eng)

kanji: もしかして彼氏ですか
hiragana: もしかして かれし です か
meaning: [Are you] perhaps [her] boyfriend? moshikashite: perhaps; possibly; maybe; by any chance; if I'm not mistaken (learn this as one word)

hiragana: きょう は げつようび だろ
meaning: [I] guess it is Monday today? getsuyoubi: Monday

hiragana: はじめて の ひとり の ばん —
meaning: [This is] the first time alone evening -> first evening where someone is alone at home. ban: evening

kanji: 真山大丈夫かゆっくり食え
hiragana: まやま だいじょうぶ か ゆっくり くえ
meaning: Are [you] ok? Eat slowly. yukkuri: slowly; unhurriedly; without haste Reminder: kuu is very casual, use "taberu" instead. Moreover, the command form (kue) is rude, don't use it. A more friendly example follows in two cards.

kanji: ねえまだ時間あるならもう少し付き合ってくれない
hiragana: ねえ まだ じかん ある なら もうすこし つきあって くれない
romaji: nee mada jikan aru nara mousukoshi tsukiatte kurenai
meaning: Hey, if [you] still have time, won't [you] give [me] the favor of hanging out a bit more? tsukiau: to keep company with; to go out with. This is often used in the context of dating, but is not restricted to this use case. Changed translation in v14 from mata - again to mada - still.
source: The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. (Eng + Jp)

kanji: いいよゆっくり食べなさい
hiragana: いい よ ゆっくり たべ なさい
meaning: It's ok. Eat slowly. yukkuri: slowly; unhurriedly; without haste

kanji: こんなに食べたら晩ご飯食えなくなるだろ
hiragana: こんなに たべたら ばんごはん くえなく なる だろ
romaji: konnani tabetara bangohan kuenaku naru daro
meaning: If [you] eat like that, dinner will become can not eat -> if you keep eating that much right now, you won't be able to eat dinner. bangohan: dinner

hiragana: きえる
meaning: kieru: to disappear; to vanish; to go away

kanji: それでは始めてください｡
hiragana: それでは はじめて ください ｡
meaning: Well then, please begin. soredeha: well then... (phrase)

kanji: 相変わらず口が悪いなムタ
hiragana: あいかわらず くち が わるい な むた
romaji: aikawarazu kuchi ga warui na muta
meaning: As always, [your] way of speaking is bad. kuchi: mouth, also: way of speaking

kanji: 私たちってそんなに有名
hiragana: わたしたち って そんなに ゆうめい
meaning: As for us, [are we] that famous? yuumei: famous, fame Don't confuse this with yuume - dream. The pronunciation is different.
source: BOFURI - Itai no wa Iya nano de Bougyoryoku ni Kyokufuri Shitai to Omoimasu (ep 1-12 w_en)

kanji: 親に心配かけちゃいけないとか
hiragana: おや に しんぱい かけ ちゃ いけない とか
romaji: oya ni shinpai kake cha ikenai toka
meaning: [You] must not cause worries for [your] parents [i.e. do not make your parents worry about something]. oya: parents; mother and father​
source: Terrace House-Boys x Girls Next Door

kanji: 真山あそこにあるの花本先生の車ですよね
hiragana: まやま あそこ に ある の はなもと せんせい の くるま です よ ね
romaji: mayama asoko ni aru no hanamoto sensei no kuruma desu yo ne
meaning: That one over there is hanamoto-sensei's car, isn't it? kuruma: car, vehicle

kanji: もしかしてあなたは人間
hiragana: もしかして あなた は にんげん
meaning: By any chance, [are] you a human? moshikashite: perhaps; possibly; maybe; by any chance; if I'm not mistaken (learn this as one word)

hiragana: げつようび の かお だ な
meaning: [It's your] Monday-face, isn't it? Who doesn't know what the Monday-face is about? In this anime, the listener has a special reason to dislike mondays, I will reveal more soon ;).

kanji: それは消えてしまうわけじゃない
hiragana: それ は きえて しまう わけ じゃない
romaji: sore ha kiete shimau wake janai
meaning: As for that [e.g. feelings someone has], it's not that [they] disappear by themselves (the "by themselves" is a consequence of -te shimau - unintended actions). kieru: to disappear; to vanish; to go away

kanji: でも私にはこの記憶がない
hiragana: でも わたし に は この きおく が ない
romaji: demo watashi ni ha kono kioku ga nai
meaning: But as for me, [I] don't have this memory. kioku: memory; recollection; remembrance

kanji: なんでこんなに有名なんだ
hiragana: なんで こんなに ゆうめい なんだ
meaning: Why is [she] this famous? yuumei: famous, fame Don't confuse this with yuume - dream. The pronunciation is different.

kanji: もう夜だしお家の人も心配するでしょうから
hiragana: もう よる だ し おいえ の ひと も しんぱい する でしょう から
romaji: mou yoru da shi oie no hito mo shinpai suru deshou kara
meaning: It's already evening and the people of her house [=her family] might be worrying [so we'd better wake her up, the conversation revolves around a sleeping person, who should go home or call home]. yoru: evening; night

hiragana: だめ だ たいじゅう が かるい
meaning: No good, [your] body weight is light / low (they are talking about reanimating someone by cardiac massage. Obviously, you need a certain body weight for this). taijuu: (body) weight

kanji: あれお箸落としちゃった
hiragana: あれ お はし おとしちゃった
meaning: Huh? [I] accidentially dropped the chopstick hashi: chopstick

kanji: でも消えるってどういうこと
hiragana: でも きえる って どういう こと
meaning: But as for disappearing, what kind of thing is it? -> What do you mean by "disappearing"? kieru: to disappear, to vanish

hiragana: きょう は げつようび だろ
meaning: [I] guess it's Monday today. getsuyoubi: Monday
